subject: POC success criteria & trial plan — Redwood POC with Atlas Payments
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Patel <sarah@atlas-payments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC success criteria & trial plan — Redwood POC with Atlas Payments

Hi Sarah / Ken (looping Ken in for visibility),

Thanks again for the time today — good conversation and appreciate the clarity on the use case (real-time transaction enrichment + merchant risk signals). Per our discussion, I summarized the proposed POC approach and the initial success criteria below so we have a single place to track decisions and next steps.

Quick recap (what we heard)
- Primary objective: reduce manual review and enrich authorization decisions with ML signals at callout time.
- Volume: expected peak ~150 requests/sec, average 40 req/sec during business hours.
- Latency tolerance: p95 end-to-end inference latency target <= 200ms.

Proposed POC scope (2 weeks sandbox -> 4 weeks trial)
- Sandbox (2 weeks): provide dedicated sandbox with sample dataset and pre-configured pipeline for evaluation and integration testing. Redwood provides sample integration test harness.
- Trial (4 weeks): run representative traffic (we can replay sampled production traces) and measure KPIs.

Success criteria / KPIs to validate (suggested)
- Latency: p95 inference latency <= 200ms on your test traffic (goal: 150–200ms)
- Throughput: sustainable peak throughput >= 150 req/sec with stable latency profile
- Cost: cost per 1k requests and cost/token estimate within your internal thresholds (we'll provide cost modeling)
- Quality: precision/recall on labeled set — target uplift relative to baseline (please share sample labels/ground truth)
- Reliability: error rate < 0.1% and no more than 2 brief incidents during trial

Owners / responsibilities
- Redwood: supply sandbox, baseline model variant, evaluation harness, sample replay tooling, monitoring dashboard (Jordan / Marissa)
- Atlas: supply sample labeled set, acceptance criteria on quality, procurement for contract terms (Sarah / Ken / procurement)

Next steps (proposed)
1) I’ll share a POC plan + estimate (attached) and a short evaluation checklist by tomorrow.
2) You share a small labeled sample (100–500 records) and any redlines for the timeline.
3) We provision sandbox access once procurement okays the trial terms.

Attachments: redwood-poc-plan.pdf (POC scope & timeline)

If that aligns, I’ll update the doc with any items you add and we’ll get procurement looped in.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182

From: Sarah Patel <sarah@atlas-payments.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Ken Zhou <ken.zhou@atlas-payments.com>, procurement@atlas-payments.com, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC success criteria & trial plan — Redwood POC with Atlas Payments

Hi Jordan — thanks for the clear recap. This looks like the right approach and the KPIs match what we discussed. A few clarifications and asks from our side: 

1) Procurement / pricing: can you include a trial estimate and a 30‑day sandbox cost summary (even if discounted)? Procurement is cc'd and will need an estimate and basic SLA language.
2) Latency: p95 <= 200ms is our hard requirement for merchant-facing calls. Can you call out expected p50/p95/p99 for the proposed sandbox config and the model variant you plan to use?
3) Throughput: 150 req/sec peak is accurate. During trial we’ll start at 20–30 req/sec to validate, then ramp to peak in controlled increments — we'll share a ramp schedule.
4) Quality: we'll share a labeled set (~250 records) by Monday — please confirm preferred format (CSV with columns: id, input, label).
5) Security/compliance: our security team will want to confirm that no production PII is stored in Redwood logs for the sandbox. I'll share the contact if they need to review evidence (SOC2).

Also looping Ken for technical validation — Ken, can you confirm the replay format and whether we should also test with 1% real traffic mirroring?

If possible, please update the POC plan with the above and include a simple evaluation checklist (owner / metric / pass threshold) so procurement can sign off quickly.

Thanks — Sarah
Sarah Patel
Head of Risk Products, Atlas Payments
sarah@atlas-payments.com | +1 212-555-0110

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Patel <sarah@atlas-payments.com>
Cc: Ken Zhou <ken.zhou@atlas-payments.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, procurement@atlas-payments.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 11:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC success criteria & trial plan — Redwood POC with Atlas Payments

Hi Sarah / Ken / procurement team —

Great — thanks for the notes. Quick responses inline below and I updated the attached estimate (redwood-estimate-v1.xlsx):

- Pricing / procurement: attached workbook includes a 30‑day sandbox cost (discounted) and a sample 4‑week trial estimate. We’ll provide a short MSA addendum for trial terms (no long contract needed for this trial).
- Latency: for the sandbox config (dedicated 2xA100-equivalent nodes, model q4_0 variant) we expect: p50 ~ 50–70ms, p95 ~ 140–180ms, p99 ~ 260–320ms depending on sequence length. We’ll instrument and share the real numbers from the pilot tests.
- Throughput: we’ll provision autoscaling to handle waypoint ramps — confirmed able to support sustained 150 req/sec with that config.
- Quality data format: CSV with columns id,input,label works great — thanks.
- Security: we do not store raw input or PII in logs by default for sandbox; we’ll share SOC2 evidence and can enable stricter retention rules for this trial. Marissa will coordinate with your security contact.

Evaluation checklist (draft) — we’ll add this to the drive link:
- Latency: p95 <= 200ms on replay dataset (owner: Redwood; pass/fail: threshold)
- Throughput: sustain 150 req/sec with p95 <= 200ms during ramp (owner: Redwood + Atlas infra)
- Cost: < $X per 1k requests (owner: Redwood)
- Quality: precision >= baseline + 10% on labeled set (owner: Atlas)
- Reliability: < 0.1% error rate during trial (owner: Redwood)

Next steps (confirmed)
1) Jordan/Marissa: provision sandbox and send credentials inside secure link by Monday EOD PT.
2) Atlas: share labeled CSV and ramp schedule by Monday EOD PT.
3) Procurement: if you can review the attached estimate and return any procurement questions, we’ll push sandbox access earlier.

Marissa — can you pick this up on security evidence and provisioning?

Thanks all — we’ll keep the timeline tight.

—
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Patel <sarah@atlas-payments.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: Ken Zhou <ken.zhou@atlas-payments.com>, procurement@atlas-payments.com
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC success criteria & trial plan — Redwood POC with Atlas Payments

Thanks Jordan — that works for us. Procurement, see the estimate attached from Redwood and the evaluation checklist below — if we can get procurement sign-off on the sandbox terms this week we’ll aim to start provisioning next Monday.

Evaluation checklist (as discussed)
- Latency p95 <= 200ms on replay dataset
- Sustain peak throughput 150 req/sec with p95 <= 200ms
- Cost modeling acceptable to procurement (see attached estimate)
- Quality uplift >= 10% on labeled set

Procurement: please advise if you need a short SOW or PO to start the sandbox trial.

Ken — please confirm the replay format (JSONL with timestamp + input) when you have a sec.

Thanks — Sarah
